description: Evaluation set for the multimodal RAG system. relevant_pages and relevant_visuals were verified by searching the extracted text of the NeurIPS PDF (11 pages) for the supporting statements; expected_keywords are groups of alternatives, each group must appear in a correct answer. An empty relevant_pages list marks a question the paper cannot answer.

queries.question: Why did the authors propose the Transformer instead of recurrent models?
How is scaled dot-product attention computed, and why are the dot products scaled?
What is multi-head attention and how many heads does the model use?
How does the Transformer encode the position of tokens in the sequence?
How many layers do the encoder and decoder stacks have, and what sub-layers does each layer contain?
How does the decoder prevent positions from attending to subsequent positions?
Which datasets were used to train the translation models?
Which optimizer and learning rate schedule were used for training?
What regularization techniques were used during training?
What BLEU score did the big Transformer achieve on the WMT 2014 English-to-German task?
How do self-attention layers compare with recurrent layers in complexity per layer and number of sequential operations?
What does the Transformer model architecture diagram show?
In the scaled dot-product attention diagram, which operations are applied to Q, K and V?
How does varying the number of attention heads affect translation quality?
On what hardware were the models trained and how long did training the big model take?
What is the inner dimensionality of the position-wise feed-forward network?
How many parameters does GPT-4 have?
